q:
I'm pregnant with my third. 

My second pregnancy was also difficult but this one is a whole different level.
cx: Third pregnancy at 33 weeks, worse than the previous two.

q: Lactation consultant and pediatrician just keep pushing EBF then sound disappointed when I talk about going back to work.
cx: Three weeks postpartum, planning feeding around a return to work at 16 weeks.

q: My lactation consultant immediately encouraged EBF again and to reduce my pumping sessions but she kept forgetting that I would be returning to work in a few months.
cx: Advice given as if she were not going back to work.

q: I feel ridiculous because 90% of people I talk to were never sick. I feel like im being overly dramatic.
cx: Nauseous since 8 weeks, now 18 weeks.

q: I keep waiting for this to get better but ever week that goes by into the 2nd trimester, it feels like this is just my new reality.
cx: Second-trimester relief not arriving at 18 weeks.

q: she was entirely unconcerned and said the baby will take what they need
cx: Her doctor's answer when told about her weight loss from sickness.

q: I’m scared of pitocin contractions and a drawn out labor, thanks to Tik Tok.
cx: First-time mother offered an early induction, scared by what she saw online.

q: I asked for an educational sheet of the induction process and what the meds and procedures look like. They didn’t have one so she hand wrote me what would be used.
cx: Recommended induction at 37 weeks over scan size and blood pressure.

q: my family has been commenting a lot recently about how underprepared I seem (in terms of baby gear). They are stressed about what happens if he's early.
cx: At 29 weeks, waited to shop until after a house move and the shower.

q: Everyone keeps insinuating I should be more stressed than I am?? Makes me wonder if I'm in denial sometimes
cx: Relieved others also shopped late.

q: Great info on the carseat discounts! Unfortunately I'm not based in the US, so no access to Target 🥲
cx: Advice in the thread assumed US shops.

q: I feel like I only ever hear the negatives (and yes, it’s hard and it’s good to talk about that too!) or see unrealistic influencers on social media touting their paid work out plans/diet regimes and what not.
cx: Second-time mother two months postpartum, posting a positive body story.

q: I’m just a mom with 2 kids rebuilding my body and it’s bringing me joy.
cx: Positive postpartum body story offered to worried readers.

q: I work overnights and typically I always drink an energy drink  And coffee to keep me up at night . I’m trying to stay away from caffeine
cx: Four weeks pregnant, night-shift worker giving up caffeine.

q: I bought mint tea but I see there is mixed reviews about drinking herbal teas.
cx: Looking for a caffeine substitute, finds conflicting advice.

q: Because influencers pack them so I assumed they were helpful. Which is not a good reason 😂
cx: Why an item was on her hospital-bag list.

q: It’s so tough to feel “prepared,” I guess we just never know our birth or baby until they get here
cx: After a long hospital-bag thread.

q: My husband’s #1 job is to DoorDash me a fancy coffee when I’m ready for it
cx: The task she has given her husband for the hospital stay.

q: He's been to 1 out of 3 of my ultrasounds bc of some unavoidable stuff
cx: At 36 weeks, fiance considering a gig during her last scan.

q: he told me goodnight and went to sleep knowing I'm upset bc he "can't help" and "doesn't know what to do"
cx: Her fiance's words after she cried for hours at 36 weeks.

q: it was in my contract that she herself would offer. Tbh the only reason my husband and I didn’t sue was because I got her covered in network so I’m in the process of getting it all reimbursed.
cx: Birth-centre midwife who did not accompany her on transfer as contracted.

q: I ended up having amazing care at the hospital, which I’m so grateful for, but I’m so frustrated at how alone and scared I was in those moments.
cx: Three months postpartum, anger at her midwife growing.
